Container.Name: deedoop
Container.Overview: deedoop: dedupe your hoard, safely. Finds duplicate files across your Unraid disks by content, whatever their names, and photos that differ only in their metadata. Read-only by default: to let it move duplicates to a quarantine or apply your plans, set /mnt to read/write, sign in as the admin and turn on changes in its Setup screen. Signed out, deedoop never changes anything. On first start, open the container's Logs for the one-time setup code that creates the admin account (or set the admin password below).

Config.Name: Disks and shares
Config.Description: Host /mnt. Read-only by default. Set it to Read/Write - Slave only if you want deedoop to remove duplicates or apply plans (also turn on changes in its Setup screen).

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Index database. Put it on the cache pool.

Config.Name: Admin password (first run only)
Config.Description: Optional. On first start, creates the admin account (user name: admin) with this password, at least 12 characters. Ignored once an admin exists; remove it afterwards. Leave empty to create the admin in the web UI with the setup code from the Logs.

Config.Name: HTTPS
Config.Description: on: serve HTTPS on the web UI port with your certificate (cert.pem and key.pem in the tls folder of the appdata) or a self-signed one deedoop makes. Then open deedoop with https:// and change the WebUI link above to https.

Config.Name: Certificate names
Config.Description: Advanced, with HTTPS on. Comma-separated host names and IP addresses to put in the self-signed certificate, for example tower.local,192.168.1.10.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Advanced. Comma-separated addresses or networks of a reverse proxy (SWAG, Nginx Proxy Manager) in front of deedoop, so it sees the real client address and HTTPS. Leave empty without a proxy.
